therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: glucose-stimulated insulin secretion and hepatic glucose metabolism
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus with inadequate glycemic control on metformin
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Change from baseline to week 6 in 24-hour weighted mean glucose

results.effect_size: Mean difference in 24-hr WMG: 0.9 mg/dL (95% CI: -7.9 to 9.6) vs glimepiride
safety_signals: MK-0941: 32 participants experienced hypoglycemia vs 37 on glimepiride (p=0.361)
1 serious AE of blood creatine phosphokinase increased in MK-0941 arm
1 serious AE of comminuted fracture in glimepiride arm

dose_info.schedule: three times daily (TID), within 15 minutes before each meal
dose_info.dose_modifications: MK-0941 titrated to maximally effective dose; metformin dose stabilized at ≥1500 mg/day and ≤2550 mg/day (or ≤3000 mg/day per local label)

context.indication: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with inadequate glycemic control on metformin
context.duration: 6-week treatment period (plus up to 4-week metformin titration/stabilization)

results_by_chain.endpoint: Change from baseline in 24-hour weighted mean glucose at week 6
results_by_chain.biology_description: glucose-stimulated insulin secretion and hepatic glucose uptake
results_by_chain.population_description: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus with inadequate glycemic control on metformin

modulation_entries.hypothesis: Metformin's suppression of hepatic glucose output provides a complementary glycemic-lowering background that could amplify MK-0941's insulin-secretory effect, but the trial showed no differential benefit of the combination over glimepiride plus metformin.
